text:
tina.cs: Heads-up  Cascade Corp reserved pool flips to green tomorrow 07:00 PT. Need final quota sanity, autoscale policy signoff, and a 25m soak. Also capture a short cost impact note for renewal deck. Who owns verification?

omar.eng: I can run the verification and validate autoscale. What's the SLA and requested headroom?

tina.cs: SLA: p95 < 210ms, errors < 0.4%. Cascade asked for 25% burst headroom first 30m and a cost cap guardrail for unexpected spikes (notify finance if >$1,200 over expected). Renewal meeting next Wed so we want clean metrics.

yuki.ops: Quota allocation in portal: us-central1-a=50, us-central1-b=30, us-central1-c=20. Commit tag cascade-2026-04-01. Finance pre-approved short +1 replica bump up to 45 minutes, approval id FIN-PRE-444.

leo.sre: Recommend autoscale policy "staged-conservative" for first 20m (scale_step=1 replica/90s) then transition to "baseline-fast". We saw kernel JIT + GC thrash with instant-burst on a similar model. Also suggest lowering OOM alert thresholds and enabling a temporary cost cap guard.

omar.eng: Plan two runs:
1) steady: 60% expected QPS for 15m to validate steady SLOs
2) burst-ramp: 0->110% in 5m, hold 10m, cool 5m to validate burst & fallback
Runner: k6 for steady, vegeta for ramp. Example k6 command:
```bash
k6 run --vus 180 --duration 15m cascade_steady.js --out json=steady.json
```

tina.cs: Please capture KV hit-rate, model cache slab occupancy, kernel/JIT logs, and cost-per-token delta. Drop artifacts to s3 and post links. I'll prepare a 1-slide summary for the renewal deck.

deploy-bot: upload: s3://redwood-ops/cascade/bringup/2165439999/steady.json

omar.eng: Steady run results: p95=195ms, errors=0.22%, KV hit-rate=84%, avg CPU 68%. Artifact: https://s3.aws/redwood/cascade/2165439999/steady-report.zip

omar.eng: Burst-ramp (staged-conservative) results: transient cold-window ~75s with p95=430ms while a node JIT'd, then settled to 205ms. errors=0.25%. artifacts: https://s3.aws/redwood/cascade/2165439999/ramp-staged.zip

omar.eng: Burst-ramp (burst-immediate) results: no prolonged cold window but CPU peaked 93% on two hosts and short GC pauses; p95 peaked 350ms, token cost +13%. artifacts: https://s3.aws/redwood/cascade/2165439999/ramp-burst.zip

leo.sre: Observations: kernel JIT on some nodes causes the longest tails; KV prefill reduces but doesn't eliminate first-kernel JIT. Warm-replica (+1) avoids JIT tails at cost bump ~10-14% during the warm window. Also note token-throttling under heavy burst can reduce latencies but increases error surface.

yuki.ops: I can enable a one-time KV-prefill lambda and set the cost cap alert (notify finance + AE) if overspend threshold hit. Portal id: quota-CASCADE-555.

tina.cs: Tradeoffs: For renewal we want minimal customer-visible blips. Recommendation: enable KV-prefill + staged-conservative autoscale for first 25m. If p95>360ms for >60s auto-fallback to warm-replica (+1) and route 5% traffic to quantized q8 fallback for safety. Add quick note in renewal slide: steady p95=195ms, burst peak p95=430ms (priming case), recommendation and cost delta estimate.

omar.eng: I'll schedule final verification at 06:10 PT and tag @leo.sre for oncall watch. I'll also include a small synthetic that exercises the top 50 prefixes to validate prefill effectiveness.

leo.sre: I'll monitor 06:40-07:40 PT and set OOM threshold at 60% memory for this tenant for the first hour. Rollback steps added to runbook: revert prefill, spin warm replica, enable fallback routing, and escalate to AE+finance if cost cap breached. Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/ops/cascade-bringup (ops doc).

yuki.ops: Prefill lambda toggled in staging and top prefixes seeded. Cost alert set at $1,200 over expected; finance notified on breach.

deploy-bot: final upload: s3://redwood-ops/cascade/bringup/2165439999/final-artifacts.tar.gz

tina.cs: Thanks all. I'll draft the one-slide renewal summary and send to @account-exec before EOD. We'll confirm customer invite for the 09:30 PT cutover call. Good job team :tada:
